newsitem.title: UK: London gold takes breather, white metals firmer.
newsitem.headline: London gold takes breather, white metals firmer.

text.p: A subdued gold market saw prices glued in a narrow range on Wednesday afternoon, but the white metals perked higher.
Bullion fixed barely changed at $349.10 an ounce, compared to $348.95 in the morning.
Prices have been stuck in a tiny $350.00-$348.20 range, with profit-taking capping the upside and physical offtake providing support, dealers said.
"It's as though the gold market is having a rest day, after the good fund buying yesterday," a dealer noted.
On Tuesday gold had dipped towards $345 an ounce, then reversed course towards $350 in late trading. But gold needed to get above $350.00 to get clear of current downward pressure, dealers said.
Such a move would also take that option strike price out of the picture for next Tuesday's over-the-counter (OTC) options expiry.
News that the Russian central bank planned to buy 90 tonnes of gold this year for reserves was positive, dealers said.
"Anything which keeps gold off the market is mildly bullish," one said.
The market showed little respond to U.S. Consumer Price Index for February which moved up moderately on Wednesday afternoon.
The CPI core rate rose 0.2 percent, in line with Wall Street estimates.
Silver, which is more technically driven than gold, stayed at the top of its similary tight $5.17-$5.21 price range.
It was indicated at $5.20/$5.22, up 11 cents from Tuesday's weak London close.
"Plays in the gold-silver ratio may still be helping silver. When gold was being sold down to the day's lows there may have been some buying in silver," a dealer said.
Platinum continued its recovery from a low around $370 on Tuesday to be indicated at $375.75/$376.75, up $4.75.
Given a relatively strong fundamental background, the metal should hold well above gold, dealers said.
Palladium was also up $4.25 at $146.25/$147.25, after bouncing smartly from Tuesday's speculative sell off which had taken prices some $10 lower.
